text:
maria: quick dump from today

maria: running RoPE scaling matrix for Mixtral-8x / Mistral-7B / Qwen-2B (linear / NTK / YARN) across seq lens 2k, 8k, 32k, 64k. TL;DR: NTK keeps ppl stable but we hit kernel fallback + KV-shard hot spots that spike p95/p999 latency for >32k.

maria: short perf snapshot (seq_len / variant / p95_ms / p999_ms / tokens_s / gpu_mem_gb)
```
2k  linear  p95=38  p999=90  420 t/s  mem=14.2GB
2k  ntk     p95=36  p999=88  425 t/s  mem=14.4GB
8k  linear  p95=62  p999=210 180 t/s  mem=20.1GB
8k  ntk     p95=60  p999=200 185 t/s  mem=20.3GB
32k linear  p95=420 p999=3.2s  35 t/s  mem=38.6GB  (observed kernel fallback on flash_attn path)
32k ntk     p95=310 p999=1.1s  48 t/s  mem=40.0GB  (stable ppl)
64k linear  p95=1.9s p999=6.4s  5 t/s  mem=70GB  (severe regressions + OOMs on some configs)
64k ntk     p95=850ms p999=2.4s  14 t/s mem=72GB (better but still variance)
```

maria: note: ppls (eval) - linear shows small perplexity improvement up to 8k then regression >32k for Qwen and Mixtral; NTK is flat across ranges. YARN between the two.

alan: can you paste the exact runtime flags / kernel preference + batching heuristics you used?

maria: sure:
```bash
MODEL=mixtral-8x
ROPE_VARIANT=ntk     # linear / ntk / yarn
ROPE_SCALE=1.0       # used 0.5/1.0/2.0 in separate runs
KERNEL_PREF=auto     # kernel selector default (auto -> tries fused then generic)
KV_SHARDS=2          # runtime-level KV sharding across two worker shards
BATCH_HEUR=latency_target=200ms,max_batch=64
WARMUP=200_tokens    # warmup to populate KV cache
```

maria: also ran with KERNEL_PREF=prefer_fused and force_fallback_for_seq>8192 to reproduce fallback.

devon: looking at the traces: the selector rejects fused kernels for >8192 because blocksize != blk_supported (we use an internal heuristic: if seq_len % 256 != 0 then fallback). That rule is too strict for Mixtral's new head dims. Selector ends up choosing generic matmul + non-streamed KV which spikes memory and latency.

devon: imagine this patch: relax modulus check to 128 and allow fused kernel for matching head dims when estimated memory < threshold. Smaller change, low risk. I can prototype.

jess: FYI: on Qwen-2B with linear RoPE at 32k we saw eval ppl increase ~2.7% vs baseline and sometimes generated token drift in long completion tests. That matches the regression notes from prod canary. NTK didn't show drift.

alan: interesting. is the ppl regression correlated with kernel fallback or with numerical instability from scaling?

maria: quick correlate: when kernel stays fused (no fallback) the ppl regression disappears. So two contributors: numerical differences in RoPE variant + implementation differences in fused vs generic kernel (different accumulation order, mixed precision shimming).

alan: workaround suggestions?

maria: short-term: force ROPE_VARIANT=ntk for Qwen and Mixtral in customer-facing Dedicated clusters for long-context >16k. Also add runtime flag `force_fused_on_large_seq=true` guarded by safety estimate (GPU mem < X) to avoid fallback.

devon: mid-term: implement selector change + add statistical consistency check in kernel selector: run small eval with a 64-token prefix when deciding to use fused path; if logits differ >eps then fall back. Cheap and prevents quality regressions.

jess: that sounds good. We should also record per-model "safe ranges" for RoPE variants in the model catalog so Console can recommend configs. I can draft recommended ranges.

maria: proposing per-model safe ranges (first pass, conservative):
- mixtral-8x: NTK recommended for seq_len > 16k; linear ok up to 8k.
- mistral-7B: linear safe up to 12k; NTK recommended >12k for stability.
- qwen-2b: prefer NTK beyond 8k (linear shows ppl regressions >8k in our tests).
- llama-family (7B/13B): linear generally stable up to 32k if fused kernels used; otherwise prefer NTK on dedicated infra.

maria: these should show up in Optimize suggestions and in rollout defaults for Dedicated private customers.

alan: batching heuristics: for long-context workloads we should bias toward smaller batch sizes + KV-prefetch to keep latency SLOs. Proposed rule: if median_seq_len > 8k -> target_batch_size = min(8, max_batch/4) and enable background KV warmup threads.

devon: kernel note: fused flash attention has better numerical stability if we do K-V accumulation in fp32 for long contexts; current implementation does mixed-precision accumulation to save memory which may cause tiny drift. Adding optional fp32 accumulation flag gives quality stability at ~1.5% mem hit.

maria: CI run summary:
ci-bot: perf/regressions ropexp-1843216789: 2 tests failed (32k-linear-ppl, 64k-linear-oom), 28 passed. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/ropexp/1843216789

sre-bot: flagged a potential customer impact on Dedicated clusters running default linear configs for Qwen on long contexts. Pager not triggered but alerts created.

jess: action items?

maria: proposed action items:
1) devon: prototype selector relaxation + small eval-in-selector (ETA 2d).
2) alan: add runtime flag to force_fused_on_large_seq + batch heuristic tweak (ETA 1d).
3) jess: craft model-catalog safe ranges + update Optimize recommendations (ETA 2d).
4) infra: schedule canary run on Dedicated for NTK defaults for Qwen/Mixtral next week.

alan: I'll pick up #2 and run a canary in staging.

devon: starting branch now. Will post PR and perf delta.

maria: thanks all. Will follow up with a concise doc for Console and Optimize changes. :white_check_mark:
